scope: Static review of refund financial safeguards and tests; tests were not executed.

assessment.coverage: Tests assert full/partial/over-request clamp behavior, same-key replay and concurrency, different-key concurrent refunds on one order bounded to order total, authorization rejection, multi-payment rejection, immutable original order data, refund-to-treasury reference consistency, conflicting idempotency state rollback, and insufficient protected drawer balance rejection.
assessment.finding: No new refund-integrity defect identified in this test file. The key different-request concurrency case is affirmative counterevidence to over-refund on one order: two distinct requests each for 15,000 against a 20,000 order are expected to post exactly 20,000 total. Source corroboration: RefundOrderHandler loads the order with UPDLOCK/ROWLOCK/HOLDLOCK and clamps against current refundable remaining inside transaction; Order.ApplyRefund independently checks amount positive and <= remaining. This does not address races across different orders sharing one account, but account balance lock is separately used in handler.
assessment.counterevidence: Server clamping bounds oversized amount, nonpositive result is rejected, refund requires authorization/approval and protected account balance, domain aggregate rejects cancelled/multi-payment and over-remaining refund. Tests support these behaviors as authored. No test here checks malformed client decimal text, and these request types are integer-piastres.
assessment.existing_crossrefs: Older client decimal rounding candidate remains bounded to at most one piastre; see financial-integrity-continuation-cashier-money-input-challenge.json. Payroll overlap and shift-close mirror items are unrelated and not reviewed.
assessment.limitations: Static inspection only. Test methods contain database query/setup calls but were not run; no live behavior, provider locking, or runtime deployment verified. No source/database modifications.
